profile.campus: Sterling, Loudoun County, Virginia (CyrusOne Northern Virginia campus, NVA1, NVA2 & NVA3)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own official facility page, this NVA1-NVA3 building (or campus) sits at 21111 Ridgetop Circle, Sterling, VA 20166 and publishes  of technical space and 44 MW of total IT capacity of technical space and 44 MW of total IT capacity. 

This facility is part of CyrusOne's broader Sterling, Virginia data center campus in Loudoun County, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn-area data center corridor described by industry press as the world's densest concentration of data center capacity. Wikipedia's entry on CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction; CyrusOne itself was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, was headquartered in Dallas, Texas, went public in 2013, and was taken private in November 2021/2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company in a deal valued at approximately $15 billion; the acquisition closed in March 2022 and CyrusOne is no longer an SEC filer for current-period results. The Sterling campus sits alongside separate NVA-numbered buildings tracked elsewhere in this registry (NVA1 through NVA9), reflecting a data center operator practice, also seen at Digital Realty, Equinix and QTS in this same corridor, of numbering sequential buildings on a shared or adjacent multi-parcel campus rather than giving each building an entirely distinct site name.

Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors has repeatedly cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a major share of the county's budget, while Dominion Energy, the region's dominant electric utility, has flagged data center demand growth in Northern Virginia as a primary driver of its own long-term transmission and generation planning; CyrusOne's Sterling campus draws power from this same regional grid alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and QTS in the same Ashburn-Sterling-Loudoun County corridor.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling, Virginia campus spans three connected buildings with 44 megawatts of published IT capacity, making it a mid-scale colocation facility in a major East Coast data center cluster.

The facility's capacity sits well below hyperscale standards but reflects the economics of the colocation model, where CyrusOne leases space to multiple tenants rather than operating as a single-tenant enterprise infrastructure. Sterling itself sits in Loudoun County, part of Northern Virginia's concentration of data centers that benefit from proximity to Washington, D.C., established telecommunications routes, and regional power availability. The 420,000 square feet across three buildings suggests substantial operational complexity, though the campus address was confirmed only through third-party aggregator sources rather than the operator's own published materials.

The data does not specify when these buildings entered service, their current utilization rate, power supply sources, or whether they serve AI workloads specifically versus general colocation demand. It also does not indicate whether the 44 megawatt figure represents nameplate capacity, available capacity, or actual draw. CyrusOne's 2022 transition to private ownership under KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners may influence future expansion or specialization, but that shift's relevance to this facility's trajectory remains unclear from the available record.
